newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Biko family names lawyers to bar S.Africa amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Biko family names lawyers to bar S.Africa amnesty.

text.p: The family of murdered anti-apartheid icon Steve Biko said on Monday it was preparing to take legal action to oppose an amnesty bid by five South African policemen seeking absolution for his death.

In the first comment by the family since the policemen applied for amnesty at the end of January, Biko's son Nkosinathi said the family met with friends and advisers on Sunday to agree on a response to the policemen's confession.
"(The family) has been and remains opposed to any application for amnesty from persons who were responsible, individually or in conspiracy, for the killing of Steve Biko," he said in a statement.
"Accordingly...it (the family) has instructed the Legal Resources Centre...to oppose the applications."
Biko, immortalised in Sir Richard Attenborough's film "Cry Freedom", died of brain damage in police detention in 1977.

The black consciousness leader became a martyr for the struggle against apartheid, and international disgust at the brutality of his death hastened white-ruled South Africa's transformation into a pariah state.
Five white officers are now seeking amnesty in return for a full confession about one of apartheid's most notorious crimes.
The Biko family has however held firm in their calls for his killers to face justice. "If you have evidence, the way to go about it is to go to court," son Nkosinathi said in a previous interview.
Biko's widow took President Nelson Mandela's government to the Constitutional Court last year to oppose the amnesty law, but failed.
The Truth and Reconciliation Commission has the power to grant amnesties to those who confess to crimes committed in the name of the apartheid system or by its violent opponents.
